title: They Loved Him More When He Was Useful
brief: A five-minute original fictional animated drama about Eli, a compulsive people-pleaser, and June, his daughter. A reserved seat at her school performance becomes the emotional anchor. Colleagues praise Eli while piling favors into his arms; each yes becomes a visible red thread. He misses June's performance while earning applause for a boss who takes his work. At home, a child's drawing shows the empty chair. The climax is a costly refusal, followed by repairing June's cardboard stage together. Sparse dialogue, original large expressive rigs, warm layered rooms, physical object exchanges and major staging changes in every shot. The psychology is dramatized as fiction, never a diagnosis. No reuse of the earlier goal-wall explainer.

cinema.note: A child searches the front row. Her wave folds against her chest when the reserved seat stays empty.
Match cut: applause elsewhere. Eli takes one more box while his boss enjoys the room.

scenes.narration: They loved him more when he was useful.

cinema.caption: Front row. Promise?
cinema.note: Earlier that morning, June runs her handmade ticket into Eli's hands. He kneels to meet her at eye level.

cinema.caption: Wouldn’t miss it.
cinema.note: Eli accepts the ticket and June throws both arms up. The promise is made through a physical exchange.
June shows the picture she has drawn: the two of them holding hands. Eli bends toward her.
A whole-body crossing carries Eli out of the warm home and into the working city.

cinema.caption: You’re the only one I can count on.
cinema.note: A colleague slumps at a desk, then extends a task as Eli approaches.

scenes.narration: You’re the only one I can count on.

cinema.caption: Of course.
cinema.note: The favor changes hands; the colleague leaves immediately. Eli stays with the weight.

cinema.caption: Quick favor. You’re a lifesaver.
cinema.note: A boss adds a delivery on top of the accepted work. His hand never asks whether Eli has room.
Another cheerful exit. The red line is now pulled taut while Eli's shoulders drop.
Eli crosses the office carrying the actual load, weaving past desks instead of gesturing at an icon.
A paper slips. Eli drops to one knee and reaches after it; the desk deadline is still behind him.
At home, Mara fixes June's costume. June practices the bow she wants her father to see.

cinema.caption: Don’t forget your seat!
cinema.note: Eli's phone interrupts the work. His exhausted face brightens at June's message.
The boss returns just as Eli begins packing. Eli hides his phone instead of naming his commitment.

cinema.caption: You wouldn’t leave the team now.
cinema.note: The boss turns a personal favor into a loyalty test. Eli grips June's ticket.

scenes.narration: You wouldn’t leave the team now.

cinema.note: A subjective shot: obligations pull him in opposing directions while the ticket remains in his hand.

scenes.narration: He had learned to hear “needed” as “loved.”

cinema.caption: Just ten minutes.
cinema.note: Eli offers the excuse to himself, then lets the boss walk away with his evening.
Time is material: the clock hand sweeps while work sheets accumulate around his body.
The curtain opens. June spots Mara, then searches the empty seat beside her.
Eli finishes the work; his boss takes the pages and receives the applause.

cinema.caption: Three missed calls.
cinema.note: A phone lights his face. The missed-call count is more important than the celebration behind him.
A desperate full-width run. The ticket bends in his clenched hand while the city slides behind him.
Eli reaches the theater and pushes through the door with his whole body.
The stage is empty. The light clicks off as Eli stops. His momentum has nowhere to go.
He kneels for the fallen cardboard star. Its cheap material makes the missed moment tangible.

cinema.caption: She kept checking the door.
cinema.note: Mara gives him June's drawing. She does not lecture. Eli reads the gap where he should have been.
Close on a parent unable to look at the drawing he has just received.

cinema.caption: Did they clap for you?
cinema.note: June is still awake. Eli lowers himself instead of trying to smile the damage away.
The question lands. Eli folds down; June turns the unused ticket over in her hands.

scenes.narration: Everyone got the best of him. She got what was left.

cinema.note: Mara sits with the hurt rather than applauding another apology. Anger turns inward.
The red strings tighten around the position where Eli stands. He finally looks at who is holding them.

scenes.narration: His kindness wasn’t the lie. His endless availability was.

cinema.caption: You’ll cover for me again, right?
cinema.note: Next morning repeats the setup. The same request now has a different cost.

scenes.narration: You’ll cover for me again, right?

cinema.caption: I can’t today.
cinema.note: A boundary is a visible hand stopping a handoff. The smile on the other face disappears.
The colleague leaves without affection. Eli has to endure the withdrawal instead of chasing it.

cinema.caption: This isn’t very team-player of you.
cinema.note: The boss tries the same pressure. Eli lets his hands come down and stays in place.

scenes.narration: This isn’t very team-player of you.

cinema.caption: My work is done. I’m going home.
cinema.note: Eli gives back the extra pages instead of bargaining for permission to leave.

scenes.narration: My work is done. I’m going home.

cinema.note: He cuts a taut red line. The other line remains for a moment: the choice is uncomfortable, not magical.
A full-width walk home. Eli is empty-handed for the first time, but not yet relieved.

cinema.caption: I missed it. I’m sorry.
cinema.note: June does not rush to forgive him. Eli meets the distance without asking her to make him feel better.

cinema.caption: It broke.
cinema.note: June offers the bent star. It is an invitation to do something, not a demand for another promise.
They repair the star together. Hands meet at the same task; time is finally being spent on her.
A cardboard box becomes a stage. Both bodies work: lifting, painting, and holding the sides together.

cinema.caption: One last quick favor?
cinema.note: The phone rings again. June stops painting and watches. The old pattern offers one last test.
He puts the phone down, face down. June's whole posture opens before he says anything.
The rebuilt little stage has an actual audience. Eli sits before the performance begins.
She does the bow from her morning practice. This time we cut to the person seeing it.
June runs from her stage into her father's arms. The action completes the opening's unanswered wave.
Their arms close. The film gives the embrace time without explaining it.

scenes.narration: Some people miss what you do for them.

cinema.note: June adds Eli back to the picture. The final object reverses the empty chair.
